I've refined `plans/functional/habit-tracker-premium-subscribe.md` into a full functional plan: 10 acceptance criteria, priority HIGH and 6 risks. It now waits for the functional review and your Gate 1 OK; I have not crossed any approval.

**Price.** The stub asked this plan to decide the monthly price. Pricing is your call, not part of the technical pipeline, so I didn't pick a number. The plan treats the price as a value you set, and no scenario fixes an amount. The question is in the status file, which is set to `needs-input`, with two options:
- **Option A (keeps building unblocked):** you decide the price in the Product Loop and it is entered as configuration before launch. The plan text stays as it is.
- **Option B:** you give me the price now and I write it into the plan. The plan text then changes, so any approval already given on it would have to be given again.

**What the plan covers.** The plan has three user stories and 10 scenarios:
- **Subscribing:**
  - The offer, one tap from the main habit screen, shows what premium includes and the monthly price.
  - The app shows premium within 10 seconds of a successful payment.
  - A declined or cancelled payment leaves the user on free, not charged.
  - A purchase interrupted after payment still ends premium and charged once.
  - Nothing can be bought while the offer can't load offline.
- **Other devices:** premium shows on any device signed in with the same account, never on a different account, and a premium user can't buy it twice.
- **Monthly renewal:** a successful renewal keeps premium with no gap. If the subscription ends because a renewal payment failed, the user is told, goes back to free, and keeps their habits and streaks.

**Issues that need your decision:**
1. **Sync has no plan.** The vision has two deliverables, subscribing and sync between devices, but only this one stub exists in `plans/`. Sync is the only benefit premium promises, so releasing subscriptions without sync would charge users for nothing. When to plan it is your decision.
2. **Cancelling isn't covered.** The vision doesn't mention cancelling, changing or refunding a subscription, and no plan covers it. Users who can't find how to stop paying will contact support.
3. **Sign-in can't be confirmed.** The project root has no app code, so I can't check whether the app has account sign-in. Showing premium on a second device needs it.
4. **Payment rules are unknown.** The vision doesn't say which platforms the app ships on, and their rules for in-app subscription payments haven't been looked up. My suggestion is that CTO Chief has `deepthink-researcher` research them before the implementation plan is written.

**Changes beyond the template:**
- I rewrote the problem statement to take the price decision out.
- I put the sections in the template's order, so Scope now comes after the acceptance criteria.
- Priority went from MEDIUM to HIGH (scored 8 out of 9).

**Three limits on what I checked:**
- None of `src/`, `docs/` or `skills/` is in this project root. That means the status-file code (`src/lib/background.js`), the downstream plan validator and `docs/PRODUCT_LOOP.md` weren't available to read. I followed the six-field status format from my brief, and checked the plan against the validator's rules as described there, not against its actual code.
- I have no clock, so the status file's last-updated time is still the old value rather than a made-up one.
- No canvas plan sits between the vision and this stub.

Summary: refined plan (10 criteria, HIGH, 6 risks), waiting on your price decision and your Gate 1 OK, and the vision's sync deliverable has no plan.

# Subscribe to premium in the app

## Problem Statement

People who use the habit tracker on two or more devices lose their streaks, because the free
app keeps habits on one phone only; in the last quarter 1,200 support requests asked for sync
between devices. The vision's answer is a paid premium plan that includes sync, but a free user
today has no way to buy premium from inside the app, so the only route to it would run through
support. This plan lets a free user subscribe to premium at its monthly price from inside the
app, and have that subscription recognized on every device they sign in on, without contacting
support. The monthly price itself is a pricing decision that belongs to the founder (Product
Loop), not to this plan: the plan uses it as a value the owner sets, and the question is raised
in this plan's status file.

## Business Alignment

**Job to Be Done:** When I track my habits on more than one device and want the same habits
and streaks on all of them, I want to buy premium from inside the app in one sitting, so I can
get sync without contacting support or starting my streaks over.

**Impact Map:**
- **Goal:** Multi-device users keep their habits and streaks across devices through a paid
  premium plan, and the requests for sync no longer go to support (vision: Problem Statement;
  first Success Criterion, "a free user can subscribe to premium from inside the app without
  contacting support").
- **Actor:** A free user of the habit tracker who uses it on two or more devices (vision:
  Target Audience).
- **Impact:** The actor buys premium themselves inside the app instead of filing a support
  request for sync. This shows up as the user's devices displaying premium after the purchase.
- **Deliverable:** An in-app subscribe flow. It shows what premium includes and its monthly
  price, takes the payment, turns the user's account premium, recognizes premium on every device
  signed in with that account, and handles the monthly renewal.

**Alignment checks:**
- The Goal traces to the vision's problem statement: YES.
- The Actor is the vision's target audience: YES.
- The Impact is observable (premium is shown after an in-app purchase, with no support contact): YES.
- The Deliverable is a single functional area (subscribing to premium): YES.

**Overlap check:** No sibling stubs. `Glob plans/functional/habit-tracker-premium-*.md` matched
1 file, this one.

## User Stories

**As a** free user who tracks habits on two or more devices, **I want** to subscribe to premium
from inside the app, **so that** I get my habits and streaks on every device without contacting
support.
Scenarios: Premium offer shows what it includes and costs; Successful subscription; Payment
declined or cancelled; Purchase interrupted after payment; Premium offer cannot load offline.
INVEST: passes. On Small: the external payment integration may not fit one Iron Loop cycle, and
the Implementation Planner splits it if it does not (Technical Risk "Payment-platform rules are
unspecified").

**As a** premium subscriber who uses a second device, **I want** every device where I sign in
with my account to recognize my subscription, **so that** I am never asked to pay twice for
premium.
Scenarios: Premium on a second device; Premium belongs to the account, not the device; A
premium user cannot buy premium twice.
INVEST: passes. On Independent: the story uses a subscription that already exists, and its tests
can start from a premium account created directly, without the first story's flow.

**As a** premium subscriber, **I want** my subscription to renew each month, and to be told
when it ends because a renewal payment failed, **so that** premium never stops without my
knowing and I pay only while I have it.
Scenarios: Monthly renewal; Subscription ended after a failed renewal payment.
INVEST: passes. Its tests can start from a premium account created directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

"The monthly price" below always means the price the owner sets (see Problem Statement). No
scenario fixes an amount.

- [ ] **Scenario: Premium offer shows what it includes and costs**
  Given a free user on a phone or tablet
  When they tap the premium offer on the main habit screen
  Then they see that premium keeps the same habits and streaks on every device they sign in on
  And they see the monthly price with its currency, and that it renews every month
  And no payment is taken until they confirm

- [ ] **Scenario: Successful subscription**
  Given a free user viewing the premium offer
  When they confirm and their payment succeeds
  Then within 10 seconds of the payment succeeding the app shows them as premium, without being restarted
  And they are charged once, exactly the monthly price the offer showed

- [ ] **Scenario: Payment declined or cancelled**
  Given a free user viewing the premium offer
  When they confirm and the payment is declined, or they cancel at the payment step
  Then they see that no payment was taken
  And they stay on the free plan with all their habits and streaks unchanged
  And they can try again from the premium offer without restarting the app

- [ ] **Scenario: Purchase interrupted after payment**
  Given a free user whose payment succeeded, but whose app lost its connection or was closed before it showed premium
  When they next open the app with a working connection
  Then within 10 seconds of opening, the app shows them as premium without their contacting support
  And they have been charged once, not twice

- [ ] **Scenario: Premium offer cannot load offline**
  Given a free user with no network connection
  When they tap the premium offer
  Then they see that the offer cannot load and that they can try again once they are online
  And they have no way to confirm a purchase, so nothing can be bought at a price they were not shown

- [ ] **Scenario: Premium on a second device**
  Given a user who subscribed to premium on one device
  When they sign in with the same account on another phone or tablet
  Then within 10 seconds of signing in, that device shows them as premium
  And they are not asked to pay

- [ ] **Scenario: Premium belongs to the account, not the device**
  Given a device where a premium user was signed in
  When a different account that never subscribed signs in on that device
  Then that device shows the free plan and the premium offer for that account

- [ ] **Scenario: A premium user cannot buy premium twice**
  Given a premium user on any of their devices
  When they open the place in the app where free users see the premium offer
  Then they see that they already have premium
  And they have no way to buy a second premium subscription

- [ ] **Scenario: Monthly renewal**
  Given a premium user whose monthly renewal date arrives
  When the renewal payment succeeds
  Then they stay premium on every device they sign in on, with no interruption and nothing for them to do
  And they are charged once for that month

- [ ] **Scenario: Subscription ended after a failed renewal payment**
  Given a premium user whose subscription has ended because a monthly renewal payment failed
  When they next open the app on any of their devices
  Then within 10 seconds of opening, they see that premium ended because the renewal payment failed
  And that device shows them on the free plan, with the premium offer available again
  And the habits and streaks on that device are still there

## Scope

### In Scope
- A premium offer one tap from the main habit screen. It states what premium includes (the same
  habits and streaks on every device the user signs in on) and the monthly price with its
  currency and monthly renewal. Scenario: Premium offer shows what it includes and costs.
- Buying premium from inside the app, with the app showing premium within 10 seconds of a
  successful payment and the user charged once. Scenario: Successful subscription.
- A declined or cancelled payment leaves the user on the free plan, not charged, with their data
  unchanged and able to try again. Scenario: Payment declined or cancelled.
- A purchase interrupted after payment still ends with the user premium and charged once, with
  no support contact. Scenario: Purchase interrupted after payment.
- No purchase is possible when the offer and its price cannot load. Scenario: Premium offer
  cannot load offline.
- Premium is recognized on every device signed in with the subscriber's account, and on no other
  account. Scenarios: Premium on a second device; Premium belongs to the account, not the device.
- A user who already has premium cannot buy it a second time. Scenario: A premium user cannot
  buy premium twice.
- Monthly renewal. When a subscription ends because a renewal payment failed, the user is told,
  returns to the free plan, and keeps their habits and streaks on the device. Scenarios: Monthly
  renewal; Subscription ended after a failed renewal payment.

### Out of Scope
- **Deciding the monthly price** (the amount, plus currencies or regional prices if any). This is
  a pricing decision owned by the founder through the Product Loop, outside the technical
  pipeline. This plan uses the price as a value the owner sets. The question is in this plan's
  status file. Before this refinement, `Grep "(?i)sync|cancel|sign[ -]?in|account|price|pricing"`
  over `plans/` found "price" in 1 file only, on the stub's former problem statement line, which
  asked for the price to be decided. No price is recorded anywhere yet.
- **Syncing habits and streaks between devices.** This is in the vision's scope, but no
  functional plan for it exists: `Glob plans/functional/habit-tracker-premium-*.md` matched 1
  file (this one), and the same `Grep` over `plans/` found "sync" only in the vision
  (`plans/done/habit-tracker-premium.md`, lines 13, 14 and 27). The owner decides
  when it is planned. See Dependency Risks.
- **Cancelling, changing or refunding a subscription from inside the app.** The vision does not
  name it, and no plan covers it: the same `Grep` over `plans/`, run before this refinement,
  found "cancel" in 0 files. The owner decides whether it is planned. See Business Risks.
- **Free trials, discounts and a yearly billing option.** Neither the vision nor the stub names
  them. They are pricing-model decisions for the founder through the Product Loop.
- **Building account sign-in, if the app does not have it yet.** No plan covers it. See
  Dependency Risks.
- **Team or family plans.** Excluded by the vision.
- **The web version of the app.** Excluded by the vision.

## Risks

### Technical Risks
- **Payment-platform rules are unspecified.** Selling a subscription on phones and tablets goes
  through an external payment system. That system's rules are not stated: which payment route
  is allowed, and how renewals, failed payments and refunds are reported to the app. The vision
  also does not name the platforms the app ships on.
  - Likelihood: HIGH. Every in-app paid subscription depends on an external payment system.
  - Impact: HIGH. A payment route the platform does not allow, or a misread rule, blocks release
    or forces a rework of the whole flow.
  - Mitigation: Confirm the target platforms with the owner, and have CTO Chief dispatch
    `deepthink-researcher` on each platform's subscription-payment rules before the
    implementation plan is written.
- **Charged but not premium.** If a purchase is interrupted between the payment and the app
  showing premium, a paying user stays on the free plan. That produces exactly the support
  request the vision wants to remove.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Test the scenario "Purchase interrupted after payment" on a real device, by
    cutting the network and by closing the app between the payment succeeding and premium being
    shown.

### Business Risks
- **The monthly price is undecided.** The stub asked this plan to decide it, but pricing belongs
  to the founder through the Product Loop. Building is not blocked, because the plan uses the
  price as an owner-set value. Launch is blocked until the price is set.
  - Likelihood: HIGH. No price is recorded in `plans/`.
  - Impact: MEDIUM. It blocks launch, not building.
  - Mitigation: Record the monthly price through the Product Loop. The question is in this plan's
    status file.
- **Users cannot stop paying from inside the app.** Cancelling is not covered (see Out of Scope).
  A user who cannot find how to stop a monthly charge contacts support, which works against the
  vision's goal.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Ask the owner before Gate 1 whether cancelling a subscription gets its own plan.

### Dependency Risks
- **Premium's only benefit, sync, has no plan.** The vision states one benefit of premium, sync
  between devices, and that deliverable has no functional plan (see Out of Scope). The scenario
  "Premium offer shows what it includes and costs" promises sync, so releasing this plan without
  sync working would charge users for a benefit that does not exist.
  - Likelihood: HIGH. There is currently no sync plan.
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Raise the missing sync plan with the owner before Gate 1.
- **Whether account sign-in exists is unverified.** Recognizing premium on a second device
  requires the purchase to be tied to an account the user signs in with. The vision says "every
  device they sign in on", but the free app keeps habits on one phone only. No app source code
  is in this project root (`Glob {src,docs,skills}/**/*` matched 0 files), so whether sign-in
  exists cannot be checked here.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH. Without sign-in, the "Premium on a second device" and "Premium belongs to the
    account, not the device" scenarios cannot be met.
  - Mitigation: Verify in the app's codebase whether account sign-in exists before the
    implementation plan is written. If it does not, raise the missing sign-in plan with the owner.

## Priority

**Priority: HIGH** (Score: 8/9)
- Dependency: MEDIUM (2). No other stub depends on this one, and it depends on none; it is the
  vision's only stub. The vision's sync deliverable is for premium users only, so a sync plan,
  once one exists, will depend on this one.
- Business Impact: HIGH (3). It delivers the vision's first success criterion directly, and it
  is the paid plan the vision's whole answer rests on.
- Technical Risk: HIGH (3). It integrates an external subscription-payment system, including
  renewals and failure reporting (Technical Risk "Payment-platform rules are unspecified").
